interpretation: Rows are scenarios, not independent bugs. Reproduction validates observed behavior; the decision evaluates usefulness and scope.

rows.scenario: daily schedules
rows.reason: Same first-time-listener calculation defect; this is a scope variant, not an independent bug.

rows.scenario: weekly plus daily
rows.reason: Same first-time-listener calculation defect; this is a scope variant, not an independent bug.

rows.scenario: pinned schedules in different zones
rows.reason: Same first-time-listener calculation defect; this is a scope variant, not an independent bug.

rows.scenario: long interval before short interval
rows.reason: Same first-time-listener calculation defect; this is a scope variant, not an independent bug.

rows.scenario: calendar before interval
rows.reason: Same first-time-listener calculation defect; this is a scope variant, not an independent bug.

rows.scenario: phased intervals
rows.reason: Same first-time-listener calculation defect; this is a scope variant, not an independent bug.

rows.scenario: eight schedules
rows.reason: Same first-time-listener calculation defect; this is a scope variant, not an independent bug.

rows.scenario: non-time listener preceding the only time listener still schedules correctly
rows.reason: The first time listener is found even when an event listener precedes it; event-only groups correctly have no next run.

rows.scenario: one cron expression with multiple hours is unaffected
rows.reason: Multiple hours inside one cron work; disabled routines correctly remain unscheduled.

rows.scenario: later invalid and too-frequent schedules pass file validation but fail API validation
rows.reason: Validate every listener through the same normalization used by the API, including the minimum interval.

rows.scenario: API-created bot routine starts correct, then unchanged file sync corrupts nextRunAt
rows.reason: Confirms normal API-created routines are affected by unchanged file sync; same two core defects.

rows.scenario: pause stays paused; resume of a single schedule is rewound to the paused period
rows.reason: Sync overwrites a valid runtime scheduling decision with historical file state. Preserve durable cadence and occurrence state.

rows.scenario: editing a single schedule is rewound to before the edit
rows.reason: Sync overwrites a valid runtime scheduling decision with historical file state. Preserve durable cadence and occurrence state.

rows.scenario: downtime catch-up is undone for single cron; historical occurrences run again on later passes
rows.reason: Sync overwrites a valid runtime scheduling decision with historical file state. Preserve durable cadence and occurrence state.

rows.scenario: downtime catch-up is undone for single interval; historical occurrences run again on later passes
rows.reason: Sync overwrites a valid runtime scheduling decision with historical file state. Preserve durable cadence and occurrence state.

rows.scenario: manual run shifts a single relative interval only after file sync
rows.reason: The pre-/post-sync discrepancy is real. Recommend manual runs leave scheduled cadence unchanged; document that policy.

rows.scenario: event delivery shifts a mixed routine's relative interval only after file sync
rows.reason: Same discrepancy for event runs. Keep event history separate from the scheduled-cadence anchor.

rows.scenario: timezone updates of a single unpinned cron are rewound by file sync
rows.reason: Sync overwrites a valid runtime scheduling decision with historical file state. Preserve durable cadence and occurrence state.

rows.scenario: invalid later file schedule aborts dispatch before a healthy unrelated routine
rows.reason: Invalid later schedules also break failure recording. Quarantine the definition and keep unrelated routines dispatching.

rows.scenario: group-owned multi-cron routine survives bot file sync and dispatches the second listener
rows.reason: Group-owned calendar routines bypass bot file reconciliation; this bounds the original defect.

rows.scenario: separate grouped-schedule validation gap: two valid listeners can fire less than five minutes apart
rows.reason: The combined schedule violates the documented five-minute floor. Recommend rejecting too-close combinations while coalescing exact coincidences.

rows.scenario: a helper-only file-sync fix must pass the installation zone explicitly
rows.reason: Pass the installation zone explicitly to the shared helper; its fallback can represent a pinned first listener. This is not another production failure.

rows.scenario: separate helper limitation: relative grouped intervals lose the longer interval's cadence, including group owners
rows.reason: Independent relative schedules need stable listener-specific anchors. Recommend independent cadence; do not pretend a helper substitution supplies it.

rows.scenario: a syntax error soft-deletes an existing routine even though its definition file still exists
rows.reason: Soft deletion is reversible, not data deletion. Keep invalid definitions visible and disabled with an error; do not silently run obsolete instructions.

rows.scenario: an unreadable automation file blocks the entire sync-then-dispatch pass repeatedly
rows.reason: The structural file fault escapes the per-routine catch and aborts sync before dispatch. Isolate reads and advance recovery past bad folders.

rows.scenario: an unreadable runs.json soft-deletes a routine whose automation.json is valid
rows.reason: History projection failure must not invalidate an otherwise valid authored definition. Recover or flag the ledger independently.

rows.scenario: legacy schedule fallback silently strips all other listeners after a malformed group edit
rows.reason: Apply legacy fallback only when no explicit trigger exists; never replace an explicitly invalid group with its first cron.

rows.scenario: crash after dispatch commit but before file projection creates a permanent duplicate-key dispatch trap
rows.reason: Stale projection rewinds a committed occurrence and repeatedly collides with its unique execution key. Same runtime-authority family.

rows.scenario: ordinary concurrent reconciliation and dispatch can erase a committed run and poison future dispatch without any crash
rows.reason: Real interleaving erases committed runtime state without any injected data corruption. Same authority/coordination defect.

rows.scenario: create rollback leaves an active ghost routine; retrying the same call ID creates a duplicate
rows.reason: Rollback plus file import loses request identity, and retry creates two active jobs. Add durable operation/projection recovery.

rows.scenario: delete rollback removes the file; later sync deletes the routine despite the DB rollback
rows.reason: The eventual delete still matches the requested operation. This establishes acknowledgement inconsistency, not a separate wrong-intent deletion bug.

rows.scenario: control: overlapping executions record one skip and preserve its lastRunAt through sync
rows.reason: Ordinary overlapping execution handling records one skip as intended.

rows.scenario: 50 backlogged routines monopolize every dispatch page and create overlap skips while a healthy bot starves
rows.reason: Starvation is driven by repeated historical rewinds. Fix that cause, then retest fairness before claiming another independent bug.

rows.scenario: file import bypasses the 50-routines-per-owner API limit
rows.reason: API and file limits differ. Decide whether trusted file imports share the cap; preserve existing configurations through migration.

rows.scenario: control: eight concurrent schedulers dispatch one occurrence exactly once
rows.reason: The existing locks dispatch a single occurrence once across eight concurrent callers.

rows.scenario: 100 live executions starve recovery of a completed execution on another routine
rows.reason: The unpaged 100-row recovery scan repeatedly selects live entries and overlooks terminal work. Rotate or paginate the scan.

rows.scenario: year-old five-minute interval exceeds dispatch transaction timeout instead of catching up in constant time
rows.reason: Catch-up is linear in missed ticks; an independent capture confirmed Prisma P2028 here. Use arithmetic advancement; the timeout threshold is machine-dependent.

rows.scenario: one unavailable event listener blocks delivery to a healthy bot on every retry
rows.reason: Per-listener error isolation is useful, but this fixture manually archives an active bot's DM. Normal retirement also disables its routines.

rows.scenario: a group dispatch handoff failure leaves a queued round stuck until startup-style round recovery
rows.reason: After a post-commit advance error, periodic recovery leaves the queued room round untouched. Retry the handoff during recovery.

rows.scenario: a late shell callback resumes an explicitly stopped and cancelled automation
rows.reason: A real late callback can pass Stop fences and queue a parent notification. Check root stop state at routing, claim and handoff.

rows.scenario: a callback queued before WakeParent remains claimable after the automation handed off
rows.reason: Merge with terminal-context fencing. It proves unnecessary continuation; most dynamic tools already reject an ended handoff.

rows.scenario: a callback with an unknown automation run ID is routed into the user-facing foreground
rows.reason: A fabricated ID in trusted callback input falls into the foreground route. Validate it; this is not evidence of external unauthorized access.

rows.scenario: a failed batched continuation is marked successful because a folded newer run was marked completed
rows.reason: A completed folded receipt masks the failed processing turn. Derive outcome from the actual executing continuation and batch relationships.

rows.scenario: an invalid Teams regex is accepted as enabled and silently never matches
rows.reason: Reject invalid patterns on save with a useful error. This is event validation, not the first-listener scheduling root.

rows.scenario: one failed follow-up launch rolls back root settlement and blocks recovery for another bot
rows.reason: Cross-bot abort is the defect. Rolling back settlement with a failed follow-up is reasonable; isolate and retry each recovery item.

rows.scenario: file imports bypass the API refusal of unscoped high-volume GitHub listeners
rows.reason: Share this policy across imports if required. File/API guardrail inconsistency is confirmed; an authorization bypass was not established.

rows.scenario: interval-first grouped schedules retain an invalid due time after a timezone change
rows.reason: Time-zone recalculation is gated by the first-derived schedule kind. Recompute from all relevant listeners.

rows.scenario: first timezone detection pins later floating schedules to the first pinned listener's zone
rows.reason: A pinned first listener's zone is not the original installation zone for later floating listeners. Preserve each listener's semantics.

rows.scenario: first timezone detection misses floating cron listeners when an interval is first
rows.reason: Same first-derived metadata defect: migration misses floating calendar listeners behind an interval.

rows.scenario: a long valid cron accepted by the schedule API is truncated and soft-deleted by file sync
rows.reason: A valid accepted expression is truncated on import. Preserve it or reject consistently at input; never truncate executable configuration.

rows.scenario: desktop prompt-only edit: Sunday represented as 7 becomes Saturday
rows.reason: Preserve the exact original trigger on unrelated edits instead of reconstructing a narrower schedule.

rows.scenario: desktop prompt-only edit: a monthly-plus-weekly rule loses its weekday
rows.reason: Preserve the exact original trigger on unrelated edits instead of reconstructing a narrower schedule.

rows.scenario: desktop prompt-only edit: an advanced rule loses its month-day constraint
rows.reason: Preserve the exact original trigger on unrelated edits instead of reconstructing a narrower schedule.

rows.scenario: desktop edit makes a valid hourly */60 cron unsavable by clamping its step to 59
rows.reason: Preserve the exact original trigger on unrelated edits instead of reconstructing a narrower schedule.

rows.scenario: desktop prompt-only edit replaces an explicitly pinned schedule's timezone with the device zone
rows.reason: Preserve the exact original trigger on unrelated edits instead of reconstructing a narrower schedule.

rows.scenario: desktop-generated triggers ignore a settings timezone override and stay pinned across later changes
rows.reason: Creation explicitly pins to the device zone, bypassing the configured override and later zone following. Use the user's resolved setting.

rows.scenario: stale desktop presentation hides a file schedule edit and restores the old time on the next prompt edit
rows.reason: Invalidate or verify presentation when the authored trigger changes; stale UI metadata must not restore old scheduling instructions.

rows.scenario: desktop prompt-only edit of a mixed event/time routine silently removes its event listener
rows.reason: Preserve the exact original trigger on unrelated edits instead of reconstructing a narrower schedule.

rows.scenario: advanced every-N-days weekday restrictions still generate weekend runs
rows.reason: The day-step branch interacts with cron DOM/DOW OR semantics. Preserve selected restrictions or reject unsupported combinations.

rows.scenario: two valid desktop cards can expand beyond the server's eight-listener limit
rows.reason: Validate expanded listeners, not just editor card count, and explain the limit before save.

rows.scenario: group routine overlap protection ends while its background shell is still running
rows.reason: The persisted running-shell fixture shows missing overlap accounting. Add real shell lifecycle coverage before finalizing the fix.

rows.scenario: control: bot routines retain overlap protection while a background shell is running
rows.reason: Bot execution settlement correctly waits for its persisted pending background shell.

rows.scenario: worker settlement rewrites event-run history as scheduled-run history
rows.reason: File history mislabels event executions as scheduled executions; runtime firing is unaffected. Low-cost accuracy follow-up.

rows.scenario: sweep: desktop round trips introduce no failure classes beyond the minimized cases
rows.reason: The Cartesian editor sweep found variants of already-minimized failures, not additional root causes.

rows.scenario: sweep: independent calendar and phased-interval invariants, seed 275
rows.reason: Independent calendar/group/phased-interval oracle passed within its eight-day comparison horizon.

rows.scenario: sweep: independent calendar and phased-interval invariants, seed 276
rows.reason: A second seed/date pass likewise found no additional timing mismatch in that corpus.

rows.scenario: coalescing a new event changes a queued bot run's prompt without changing its recorded revision
rows.reason: The queued inbox executes a different prompt from its recorded immutable revision. Freeze it or explicitly transition the execution revision.

rows.scenario: control: coalescing a group event preserves the queued execution's original instruction
rows.reason: Group coalescing preserves the pending execution's saved prompt, supporting the intended snapshot invariant.

rows.scenario: a prompt-only update resets a group interval's due time without any file reconciliation
rows.reason: Even without files, metadata-only updates re-anchor relative intervals. Preserve next-run state when scheduling state did not change.

rows.scenario: an uncertain create retried with edited input silently returns the original routine
rows.reason: Returning the original receipt for the same key is normal. Fix changed-payload conflict/recovery in the form/API; blind key rotation risks duplicates.

rows.scenario: a UUID-shaped folder can make a different routine resolve when addressed by UUID
rows.reason: Resolve an existing UUID before slug fallback. The observed wrong winner depends on SQL plan/order; unguarded agent mutations are affected.

rows.scenario: a run fired by a later schedule is described to the model as firing on the first schedule
rows.reason: The correct later-listener dispatch is isolated before sync overwrites it. Fix its misleading description alongside multi-schedule support; it is not another missed-run proof.

rows.scenario: Advanced Every 45 minutes alternates 45- and 15-minute gaps
rows.reason: Cron */45 is correct cron but does not implement an elapsed 45-minute promise. Change the editor representation or supported choices.

rows.scenario: Advanced Every N days discards selected month days
rows.reason: Same day-step restriction-loss family as the weekday case. Do not count this as another independent bug.

rows.scenario: Advanced summaries omit selected months
rows.reason: The actual month-restricted timing is correct; the summary is misleading. Fix as a small UI accuracy task.
